editorial.headline: Agricultural Machinery Wholesale: Open Nationally, Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This wholesale activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but a permanent Bali moratorium prevents PMA registration there today.
editorial.body:
A foreign-investment company cannot register this agricultural and forestry machinery wholesale activity in Bali today. That is the practical starting point, despite a nationally open foreign-investment position with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. In Bali, the activity is blocked by the province’s permanent, island-wide moratorium on PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. At the Besar scale, OSS assigns Low or Medium-Low risk across every stated scope of this activity, bringing it within that restriction.

The commercial substance is wholesale trade in the working equipment behind farming and forestry. It includes ploughing equipment, fertiliser spreaders and seed planters; harvesting and threshing equipment; milking machinery; machinery for poultry and beekeeping operations; tractors used in agriculture and forestry; and lawn-mowing machinery. This is therefore an equipment-trading activity rather than a farming operation itself: its centre of gravity is the wholesale supply of machines and tools used across cultivation, livestock-related work, harvesting, and forestry. Its stated boundary is also clear: wholesale trade in fertilisers and agrochemical products, and wholesale trade in animal feed, sit outside the scope.

The activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. Nationally, it is marked TERBUKA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100% under the cited presidential regulations. That national openness is real, but it is not a route around Bali’s local PMA restriction. For a founder considering Bali as the registration location, the decisive fact is not the national ownership ceiling but the Bali classification outcome: the relevant risk treatment triggers the permanent moratorium. The result is straightforward—this activity may be nationally available to a fully foreign-owned company, yet it cannot be registered as PMA in Bali under the current provincial rule.

That distinction matters because the activity’s commercial identity remains broad and recognisable: it serves the wholesale movement of agricultural and forestry machinery across the full chain of field preparation, planting, harvesting, livestock systems, and grounds maintenance. But location changes the registration answer. National openness does not overcome the island-wide Bali moratorium.
